title: The NOLA label photo: officers and Quezergue's role
summary: Looking at a 1962 photo, he lists NOLA's officers and attorney and says he was arranger and recording director, unsure of timing relative to Mr. Big Stuff.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I was looking at this in 62, for the NOLA library. I recognize you sitting at the desk with her.

Yeah. I'm trying to think. Okay, Robert Collins, he was our, he was our, Robert Collins was our attorney. That's where his name come in. You look, why do you look at me, the medallions? I think this came after Malico, didn't it?

Yeah. I think that came after Mr. Big Stuff. I'm not sure. Uh, we might have had the company the same time I was doing work with Dave. Maybe that's what it is. I just don't recall. It was October 13th, 1962.
Yeah. But what, but I'm looking at all this, they obviously put a label together. Yeah. And what was your, what was your role at NOLA?
I was the music director, I would imagine you would call me. In the other position I probably didn't want to hear about. Let me take care of the A&R, I guess.
So what was, did you all have a, any formal arrangement there? I mean it looks pretty formal. You, there's five guys sitting at the table.
Yeah, but the fifth guy is the attorney.
Okay, Robert Collins, who was the, who was the judge. Right. Who became the judge, I think, yeah.

Yeah. All right, uh, well Eugene was the treasurer. Ulis Gaines was the president. What, Ulis Gaines? Uh, Robert Collins was the legal, uh, Clinton Scott was the vice president. Wardell Cazare, arranger, recording director. That's, that's what I was. Okay. That's what I wanted to be because now I have someone that can take care of the business in and out to concentrate on my music. Okay. But I can't recall if that was before or after Mr. Big Stuff. No, Big Stuff.
That was before Mr. Big Stuff. I'll tell you what.
